additionalCoursework: A course in oral communications (speech, interpersonal communication, etc.) is recommended. Information about our prerequisite courses can be found at this link: https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/prospective-students/admissions

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: MCW prides itself on being an inclusive community where all people are valued and have a voice – this is essential to our ability to be a national leader in academic medicine. Inclusion is about recognizing, honoring and ultimately leveraging our differences to build a better community. We define diversity as a commitment to understanding and embracing our innate differences and unique experiences to foster a sense of belonging for all. The diversity of MCW will continue to be an important source of innovative ideas and creative accomplishments. We affirm our commitment to individual merit, fairness and equal treatment in all aspects of academic and institutional decision-making, while also providing an environment that celebrates both personal and collective achievement.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a temporary withdrawal for a number of reasons, educational or personal. A temporary withdrawal will not be granted for a period in excess of one year. Renewals may be approved on a yearly basis for students enrolled in other degree programs. An exception to this pertains to students in the Medical Scientist Training Program, where a three year withdrawal can be granted for the PhD portion of the program. A temporary withdrawal from the MCW-Green Bay or Central Wisconsin programs will almost certainly result in graduation being delayed.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
MCW encourages its students to enjoy a well-rounded lifestyle with a variety of personal and professional programs. Student life is enhanced by more than 60 student organizations and interest groups providing opportunities for professional and leadership development, community service, and recreation. Support services include individual and group advising, tutoring support, preparation for licensure exams and career counseling for residency training. 

Please visit: https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/current-students/student-affairs/student-organizations-interest-groups
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The MCW-Milwaukee campus is located in the Milwaukee Regional Medical Center, in a suburb seven miles west of downtown Milwaukee. MCW-Milwaukee offers a safe, comfortable environment to live and study, with easy access to the city and its amenities and opportunities. 
Please visit: https://discoverwauwatosa.com/
Please visit: https://www.visitmilwaukee.org/

The MCW-Green Bay campus is based at St. Norbert College in De Pere, WI, a suburb seven miles from the Green Bay city center. Basic science and clinical facilities and opportunities are located throughout the greater Green Bay and De Pere area. 
Please visit: https://www.greenbay.com/plan-your-visit/communities/de-pere/

The MCW-Central Wisconsin campus is based near Aspirus Hospital in Wausau, WI, with clinical facilities and opportunities located throughout the region. 
Please visit: https://www.visitwausau.com/
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Student housing is not provided; however, MCW provides resources about local housing options and assistance with roommate matching. Student-led groups on social media platforms are typically organized to help incoming students connect. 

Please visit: https://www.mcw.edu/education/academic-and-student-services/student-housing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
Campus organizations and interest groups are available including the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender People in Medicine (LGBTPM) organization. Please visit:
https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/current-students/student-affairs/student-organizations-interest-groups
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: MCW supports applicants and learners with disabilities through the Office for Student Accessibility (OSA). OSA works collaboratively with students to determine reasonable accommodations based on documented functional needs in academic, clinical, and testing environments. Services may include exam accommodations, clinical access supports, assistive technology consultation, and coordination with national testing entities when appropriate. MCW is committed to an interactive, individualized process that promotes equal access while maintaining essential program standards. Students are encouraged to engage with OSA early to support timely planning. If you have additional questions, please contact Jason Anderson, Accommodations Manager, at jaanderson@mcw.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The MCW Student Assistance Program provides 10 counseling sessions per presenting issue, financial consultation, legal consultation, and more - all at no cost to the student. 

The MCW Department of Student and Resident Behavioral Health offers an additional 10 unbilled counseling sessions per academic year. These sessions can be talk therapy and/or medication management/psychiatric services. 

SilverCloud is a free, self-guided, interactive mental health resource offering online programs for anxiety, depression, and stress, available to all MCW students. 

The Office of Student Health & Wellness also offers and facilitates many other services, including wellbeing coaching or navigation, a wellness podcast, various programming and events, support groups, and a wellness Brightspace course. 

All three MCW campuses have a Student Food Center for the purpose of addressing food insecurity among students by providing free food and hygiene items for students year-round. All three campuses also have partnerships with local animal foster programs, allowing students to foster an animal for a short period of time. 

MCW wants to offer you the best technology experience by providing the tools and services you need to excel. Incoming students will be provided with an enterprise class laptop computer, fully configured to MCW hardware and software standards.

Please visit the following links for even more information about our wellness programs and resources: 
Office of Student Health and Wellness: https://www.mcw.edu/education/academic-and-student-services/student-wellness
Student Health & Wellness Resources: https://www.mcw.edu/education/academic-and-student-services/student-wellness/student-health-and-wellness-resources
Department of Student and Resident Behavioral Health: https://www.mcw.edu/departments/student-and-resident-behavioral-health
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: MCW Medical School has an exceptionally collaborative campus culture. Several factors contribute to that, including the pass/fail grading system employed during the foundational science years with no internal ranking of students. Additionally, MCW is a freestanding medical school and not affiliated with any undergraduate institution. This results in a very low student-to-faculty ratio which supports ample opportunities like research or shadowing as the faculty are focused on medical and other professional students only, not undergraduate students. As a health sciences institution, students have the opportunity to learn alongside other professional students pursuing healthcare careers at MCW and local institutions through interprofessional education efforts. A common phrase spoken around campus is the “MCW Family,” which truly encompasses the supportive, collaborative, and caring nature of our students, faculty, and staff.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students are required to have a government-issued ID card, especially for rotation at the VA and other clinics. The most common government-issued ID is a driver's license, but other documents may be used in place of that. Having a vehicle is highly recommended at the Milwaukee campus and is required at both Regional Campuses. In Milwaukee, students can be placed in any clinic/hospital within a 30-mile radius. Public transit is available but timing and routes are difficult to manage.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students must have a clean and professional appearance and adhere to the guidelines of clinical partners. Any clothing or personal accessories that interfere with patient care are unacceptable.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: We provide academic advising, peer tutoring, academic enhancement, step preparation and clinical advising. Please visit: https://www.mcw.edu/education/academic-and-student-services/academic-support
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction in their first few weeks of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group case-based learning is supplemented with traditional lecture, hands-on lab sessions, virtual activities, self-directed learning, and learning with patient care teams and patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Phase 1: longitudinal clinical experience with a preceptor. Phase 2: clinic, hospital, and procedure based core clinical clerkships. Phase 3: supports career & internship prep. Electives available.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required for sessions designed for teamwork, collaborative learning, and clinical skills development. Other teaching activities can be completed asynchronously and virtually.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The MCWfusion Curriculum was implemented in July 2023 after a lengthy and thorough development process with meaningful involvement of countless faculty, staff, and students. The overarching goal of the curriculum is to support students’ development into competent well-rounded physicians who will be excellent clinicians in any specialty - prepared to practice in the rapidly evolving health care environment as life-long learners and develop skills for specific career goals. Foundational sciences, clinical medicine, and character and professional development are integrated across three phases. The organ system-based Phase One is “inquiry-based” and engages learners to learn from patient-based cases. Early direct patient care experiences are supplemented with classroom and simulation activities. Required clinical clerkships comprise Phase Two, and Phase Three provides guided exploration of career paths and preparation for internship. Students learn with peers, staff, and faculty coaches across all phases in our learning communities and pursue their own interests in one of eight Scholarly Concentrations.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
All students interact with primary care practitioners (PCPs) during Phase 2, especially in the ambulatory care integrated clerkship. In addition, many PCPs serve as mentors/preceptors through Clinical Apprenticeship, Scholarly Concentrations, and Learning Communities. Phase 3 will also include primary care/ambulatory electives. Having multiple educational sites in Wisconsin allows MCW to effectively pursue its education missions through offering diverse curricular tracks.

A goal of MCW-Green Bay and MCW-Central Wisconsin is to contribute to ameliorating predicted physician shortfalls in primary care. Thus, the three-year curriculum option emphasizes those specialties needed for providing primary care where shortages have been identified including primarily family medicine and psychiatry. Students attending MCW-Green Bay and MCW-Central Wisconsin should have a deep interest in practicing in WI and serving the needs across the state. A four-year curriculum option can also be pursued.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Research is one of MCW's four core missions thus vast opportunities exist for students to be involved in research during their time at MCW-Milwaukee. Through the Scholarly Concentrations program, the Medical Summer Student Research Program (MSSRP), and individually, students can pursue opportunities at all levels of research - from basic science/bench experiments to clinical cohorts to population-level, health policy studies. Opportunities are individualized and can range from summer exposure to longitudinal involvement through all four years of medical school enrollment.  

The MSSRP offers a number of full-time, paid research training opportunities to MCW medical students enrolled on the Milwaukee campus during the summer between M1 and M2 years. Trainees are integrated into the research teams of full-time, MCW faculty preceptors working on basic science, clinical or translational research. Please visit: https://ctsi.mcw.edu/education/pre-doctoral-programs/sams
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community engagement is one of our four mission areas, and we are a Carnegie CE Classified campus. Many optional service opportunities exist through student groups and the Scholarly Concentrations.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students are not required to complete a thesis. Every medical student is required to participate in and present the results of a scholarly project.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: MCW is affiliated with Children’s Wisconsin, Froedtert Hospital, and Zablocki VA Medical Center in Milwaukee as well as many other hospitals and clinics in Eastern and Central Wisconsin.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: MCW employs a Pass/Fail grading system for Phase One and tiered grades (honors/high pass/pass/fail) for Phase Two and Three.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: Instruction is delivered using the English language.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The Medical College of Wisconsin (MCW) is a private, freestanding medical school with three campuses, one located on the Milwaukee Regional Medical Center grounds, one in the greater Green Bay area at St. Norbert College, and one in Central Wisconsin, based in Wausau near Aspirus Hospital. MCW maintains strong relationships and educational programs with affiliated teaching hospitals statewide. MCW also has numerous other educational offerings including a Graduate School, Pharmacy School, and Master of Science in Anesthesia (MSA) program. Additionally, MCW is the largest private research center in Wisconsin and ranks in the top 100 out of 20,000 research institutions in the nation. 

More great information can be found here: https://www.mcw.edu/-/media/MCW/About-MCW/MCW-Facts-and-Impact-2025-Standard.pdf
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our Mission: We are a distinguished leader and innovator in the education and development of the next generation of physicians, scientists, pharmacists and health professionals; we discover and translate new knowledge in the biomedical and health sciences; we provide cutting-edge, collaborative patient care of the highest quality; and we improve the health of the communities we serve.

Our Vision: Pioneering pathways to a healthier world.

Our Values: We strive for excellence in education, research, patient care, and community engagement by acting in caring ways, engaging in collaborative efforts, approaching our world with curiosity, advancing inclusive practices, demonstrating integrity in all we do, treating everyone with respect. 

Many aspects of the MCWfusion Curriculum connect directly to our mission. Doctoring Threads create opportunities for students to obtain the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to be successful clinicians. Spiral Weeks allow students to create and act on individual development plans for excellence and remediation and develop meaningful connections with peers and faculty. Learning Communities become a longitudinal support system during medical school. Students interact with a small group of peers and a faculty navigator while nurturing their adaptive learner skills and obtaining academic advising and coaching.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes - a criminal background check is conducted for all applicants offered admission and again for matriculating students. This includes the WI Caregiver background check.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants admitted during regular cycle: April 30, 2027. Applicants admitted from the waitlist will be given deadlines on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
The undergraduate letters of recommendation are required unless your undergraduate degree conferral was at least five years ago.

Letters from Principal Investigators may be submitted as optional letters, but typically cannot fulfill the undergraduate or graduate letter requirements.

If you are applying to the MD/PhD (MSTP) or MD/MS program, it is strongly recommended that you include a letter of recommendation speaking to your ability to become a physician-scientist.

For more detailed information, please visit: https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/prospective-students/admissions
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Required Undergraduate Academic Letters: You must submit 2 letters from classroom professors, at least 1 of whom must have taught biology, chemistry, physics, or a comparable science discipline. We will also accept a committee letter or packet of letters.

Required Graduate Academic Letter: ONLY if you are currently or have previously been enrolled in a degree-granting graduate program, you must submit 1 letter of recommendation from a professor or thesis advisor.  Students recently accepted to or matriculated into a graduate program are not required to submit a letter.

Additional Professional Letters (optional but encouraged): You may submit up to 3 additional letters of recommendation. These letters are optional but encouraged. For optimal consideration, these should be received by MCW before the application is complete.

Total number of letters accepted will be 5 (2 undergraduate and 3 optional) or 6 (2 undergraduate, 1 graduate, 3 optional), depending on the applicant's situation.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
When invited to interview, you will also receive additional information via your secondary application portal and through email communications.

Please visit our website or contact our office for additional information. https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/prospective-students/admissions

medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat:
Varies by campus location:
-MCW-Milwaukee: two 1-1 open file interviews with student and faculty interviewers. 
-MCW-Central Wisconsin and MCW-Green Bay: one open file interview with a large panel including community members, students, and faculty.

medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interview day programming and interviews will be conducted virtually using Zoom.

medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Highly competitive applicants who are strongly interested in the Regular MD program are encouraged to apply Early Decision. The EDP is available at all campuses but not dual-degree programs.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: MCW-Milwaukee: None. MCW-Central Wisconsin and MCW-Green Bay: state residency, connections to WI and/or demonstrated commitment to practice medicine in WI are considerations in the selection process.

medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: All applicants must meet eligibility requirements.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: MCW will accept applications from US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and DACA recipients only. All must meet eligibility requirements.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: MCW will accept applications from US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and DACA recipients only. All must meet eligibility requirements.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: MCW will accept applications from US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and DACA recipients only. All must meet eligibility requirements. DACA recipients must complete a Certification of Finances form.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Please visit our website or contact our office for additional information: https://www.mcw.edu/education/medical-school/prospective-students/admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: When there are multiple MCAT scores, we will combine the best section scores from the two most recent eligible exams to create the best overall score. All lifetime scores will be visible as well.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: MCAT score(s) will be reviewed as one part of a holistic review process. An MCAT score of at least 500 is strongly encouraged. This is not a required minimum, and applicants with lower scores may still be considered based on the strength of other application components. While applicants with a wide range of scores are admitted, applicants are advised to review the mean and median scores of successful applicants at schools where they choose to apply.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: GPAs will be reviewed as one part of a holistic review process. Individual course grades, prerequisites, timing and breadth of coursework, and grade trends are all considered in the context of the other application materials. While applicants with a wide range of GPAs are admitted, applicants are advised to review the mean and median scores of successful applicants at schools where they choose to apply.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: No minimum. We will consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework regardless of undergraduate GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: No minimum. We will consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework regardless of number of credit hours.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework completed at a community college will be accepted, regardless of pathway, and reviewed as part of a holistic review process and in the context of the other application materials. While prerequisite coursework may be completed at a community college, applicants should ensure they have obtained mastery of the course material regardless of the institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may upload any supplemental information directly onto their secondary application portal when they gain access. They are able to do so via the "Document Upload" section. Anything added to that section of the portal will be reviewed alongside the rest of their application materials. These additional materials are not only accepted, but encouraged.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Technical Standards for Admission, Retention, Promotion and Graduation consist of the minimum physical, cognitive and emotional requirements to provide reasonable assurance that students can complete the entire course of study and participate fully in all aspects of medical training. Incoming medical students and continuing medical students are required to attest that they meet these requirements before matriculation and prior to MCWfusion Phase Two, respectively. Medical students are required to promptly notify the Associate Dean for Student Affairs if their ability to meet the standards has temporarily or permanently changed.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Most financial assistance offered is in the form of loans from the Federal Direct Loan programs. U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens are eligible to participate in these federal student aid loan programs. MCW has a very limited pool of institutional scholarships and loans based on merit and/or need. Applicants are encouraged to send their FAFSA to MCW and begin the financial aid application process as soon as they are interviewed. 

To matriculate, all students must submit a Financial Planning Form. International and DACA applicants must file proof of financial support when accepting their offer of admission. 

Please visit the Financial Aid Information for New/Prospective Students page of our website for more information: https://www.mcw.edu/education/academic-and-student-services/financial-aid-and-tuition/new-prospective-students
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Students enrolled on the MCW-Milwaukee campus will generally pay four years of tuition, while students enrolled at the Green Bay and Central WIsconsin campuses will generally pay three years of tuition. In-state tuition number listed below does not reflect Wisconsin Medical Student Tuition Assistance that is applied to all Wisconsin resident tuition. That amount has yet to be determined for the 2016-17 school year.

medSchoolPrograms.name: MD/MS in Clinical and Translational Science
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Applicants interested in the MD/MS program must apply to MCW Medical School using the “Combined MD/Graduate” program type.  Concurrent acceptance to MCW’s Medical School is required to matriculate into the MD/MS program. Applicants may still be considered for MD admission should the MD/MS program decide not to pursue their application further.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
MD/MS in Clinical and Translational Science: If you wish to pursue a medical career with a research focus, this program was designed for you. In just four years, you will earn both your Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree and a Master’s degree in Clinical and Translational Science (MSCTS), giving you a solid foundation in both patient care and research. 

From day one, you will dive into the core courses for the MSCTS, laying a solid foundation for research. As you progress through MD Phases 2 and 3, you will have the chance to tailor your studies with electives and work on your Master’s thesis research. The curriculum spans the entire translational research continuum (T0 to T5), equipping you with innovative skills in translational research, clinical statistics, epidemiology, ethics, safety, and study design.

Whether you are driven to improve patient care or advance medical science, this program offers the support and structure to help you make a real impact.

MMP: The mission of the MMP is to provide promising college graduates with the opportunities they need to gain admissions to medical school, other health professional programs, or biomedical jobs. Our program includes MCW School of Medicine courses and exams, providing students with experience comparable to MCW medical students. Our program also includes MCAT preparation and conditional admissions interviews to the MCW School of Medicine. 

Summer Programs (Health Science and Medical Career Pathway Programs): The Medical College of Wisconsin hosts several programs that support learners in their academic and professional journeys in medicine and biomedical science, providing opportunities to engage with many MCW departments and even partner with other institutions and organizations in the community. These programs are offered during both the academic year and summer. Review the website to find the best opportunities based on education level and time of year.

medSchoolPrograms.name: MCW Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Applicants interested in the MD/MPH degree must first apply to MCW Medical School using the “Regular MD” program type. After matriculating, you will be eligible to apply for the dual-degree MD/MPH program during the spring of your M1 year.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: A goal specific to MCW-Central Wisconsin and MCW-Green Bay is to contribute to ameliorating predicted physician shortfalls in primary care. Thus, the three-year curriculum option available at those campuses emphasizes those specialties needed for providing primary care where shortages have been identified. This includes primarily family medicine and psychiatry.
medSchoolMdPathway.spotAvailable: Typically, 20-25 students matriculate at each regional campus (MCW-Central Wisconsin and MCW-Green Bay) each year. The majority of each incoming class are Wisconsin residents; however, out-of-state applicants who are a strong mission fit and/or have a Wisconsin connection are encouraged to apply and matriculate.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Eligibility is the same across all three MCW campuses.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Application deadlines are the same across all three MCW campuses.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess:
The application process is the same across all three MCW campuses. 

The secondary application will ask applicants to choose which MCW campus location(s) they'd like to apply to. If they choose multiple campuses, they'll be required to rank the locations in a preference order. The application is exactly the same for all applicants with two additional essay questions required of those applying to the Central Wisconsin or Green Bay campus locations.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Students attending MCW-Central Wisconsin and MCW-Green Bay should have a deep interest in primary care and/or psychiatry as well as practicing in Wisconsin and serving the needs across the state.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: 100-200 at MCW-Milwaukee and 25-50 at MCW-Green Bay and MCW-Central Wisconsin.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are placed on the waitlist throughout the interview cycle with few offers extended prior to May. The waitlist is unranked, and applicants are selected through a holistic review process.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
MCW applicants are expected to have a strong educational foundation in the sciences. Additionally, students are expected to have completed courses in math, English, and the social sciences (psychology or sociology). Prerequisites must be taken at a regionally accredited institution in the United States or Canada. AP and CLEP credit is accepted for some requirements. IB credit is not accepted.

We will accept pass/fail grades for coursework, including prerequisites, taken during the COVID-19 pandemic only (including January 2020 – Summer Term 2023).

Beyond undergraduate courses, applicants are expected to have demonstrated leadership skills, strong communication skills, and a solid orientation to the profession of medicine.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites:
Twitter: @mcwmedschool
Facebook: Medical College of Wisconsin Admissions Office
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: All previous prerequisite coursework will be reviewed and can be deemed acceptable. It is recommended that applicants retake courses if they have not retained mastery of the course content.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Student selection is based on a careful analysis of the suitability for the medical profession. Academic achievement, MCAT scores, and Casper score are evaluated. Subjective factors include the personal statement, essays, experiences, recommendations, and interviews. Interviews are integral, specific to each campus location, and required before acceptance. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis by date of completion. Interviews are conducted and offers are made on a rolling basis until the class is filled. Applicants are encouraged to complete the application in a timely manner. Early submission (prior to August 15) of all supporting material and completion of the secondary application will enhance an applicant's chance of receiving an interview and subsequent offer of admission.

For MCW-Green Bay and MCW-Central Wisconsin applicants ONLY: MCW seeks to identify candidates with a demonstrated commitment to practicing primary care or psychiatry in Wisconsin.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Physician shadowing is highly recommended in addition to other medical/clinical and patient care experiences.
